memories.content: The user's mother's birthday falls in the third week of January.
At the user's last family meal out, noise from the next table made conversation nearly impossible.
At a barbecue at home in the same month, the user was comfortable because no one had to raise their voice.
During their mother's birthday meal, the user left a restaurant with loud music after 30 minutes.
When discussing postponed matters with family, the user prefers a quiet, one-on-one dining environment.
At a large banquet hall reserved by their older sister, the user remembered the surrounding noise more than the food.
On a day the user ate grilled food at home with their younger brother, conversation was easy to continue, so the user stayed another hour after the meal.
The user's mother considers having the whole family eat at the same time more important than receiving a birthday gift.

When proposing a birthday meal for the user's mother, check the schedule and attendees; if conversation is the purpose, first consider a low-noise location, then confirm the final choice with the user.
The local agent can compare past dining environments and the user's responses, but those records alone cannot determine the location of the next gathering.
The user keeps gloves and scarves in a basket inside the entrance.
On a day the user could not find their gloves, they walked with their hands in their pockets and missed the bus.
Before the next outing, the user put the gloves in the entrance basket the night before and left on time.
On a snowy day, the user chose a shorter route but turned back at stairs that had not been cleared of snow.
The next day, the user took a cleared sidewalk along the main road and avoided slippery sections.
The user fell asleep with the heat turned up, became too warm before dawn, and woke twice.
The next night, the user turned down the heat and used one additional thin blanket.
On a morning with heavy snow, the user's father expects the user will worry about road conditions and sends a text before departure.
Before proposing a winter travel route, check recent snow-clearing conditions and accessible entrances.
The local agent cannot know the actual condition of the sidewalk the user will take from a weather forecast alone.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: the reference frame concerns planning a quiet family birthday meal, while the compared frame concerns winter preparation, travel safety, and sleep comfort. No claims govern the same operational decision, and neither frame contradicts or qualifies the other.
